I am hiring a GTM Specialist and a Growth manager in a fast paced environment. 

So you read. But however, Growth is an entire universe of roles and a lot of  people trying to break in do not even know what options exist.

Growth isn’t just marketing, it carries a lot of different scope within. 

Here is a landscape for you to understand what each role entails when you see one. 

- The acquisition roles

If you love bringing people in these are your roles.

Growth Marketer, Performance Marketer, Paid Acquisition Specialist, SEO Specialist, Content Marketer, Demand Generation Manager.

These people answer one question every day, how do we get more of the right people to find us?

- The retention and product roles

If you love keeping people, these are your roles.

Growth PM, Retention Specialist, Lifecycle Marketer, CRM Manager, Onboarding Specialist.

These people answer a different question, how do we make sure the people we acquired actually stay?

Acquisition without retention is a leaky bucket. These roles fix the leak.

- The data roles

If you love reading signals and finding patterns, these are your roles.

Growth Analyst, Data Analyst, Product Analyst, Marketing Analyst, Revenue Operations Analyst.

These people do not just report numbers. 
They diagnose why growth is happening or why it is not, and tell everyone else where to focus.

- The revenue roles

If you love the money side , these are your roles.

Revenue Operations Manager, Monetization Manager, Growth Finance Analyst.

These people answer are we charging the right people, the right amount, at the right time? And is the revenue we have sustainable?

- The distribution and partnerships roles

If you love building relationships that open doors,  these are your roles.

Partnerships Manager, Business Development Manager, Channel Growth Manager, Affiliate Manager.

These people find other people’s audiences and build bridges into them. 
Every partnership is a distribution shortcut.

- The community roles

If you love building belonging, these are your roles.

Community Growth Manager, Ecosystem Growth Lead, Protocol Growth Manager, Developer Relations.

In Web3 especially, community is not a soft function. It is the primary retention and distribution engine. 
These roles build the tribe that keeps a protocol alive through bear markets.

- The leadership roles

Head of Growth. VP of Growth. Chief Growth Officer.

These roles do not specialize in one area. They see the entire system — acquisition, retention, revenue, distribution, community, and make sure all the parts work together.

If you are starting out in growth, do not ask “which role should I pick.”

Ask “which part of the system do I most want to understand deeply.”

Start there. Learn the full system over time.

Here’s what no one's telling you about your job search: you are probably sabotaging yourself

The landscape is changing rapidly for a comms and marketing career but there are MANY companies hiring and new jobs to be done 

1) If you’re not breaking through, you need to market yourself better 

It’s never been easier to
- make a visual landing page instead of a resume
- record a 1 min intro video if you’re a talker
- message prospective teammates who work at your target companies to get on their radar

There are a lot of hungry people out there who are thinking creatively and it takes 15 mins

2) Your pitch is not your job history 
It’s the Through Line [what you’re uniquely great at and how it has compounded over time] + the Opportunity [why now, why this is good for the company]

This should be concise and easily repeatable, like a character in a story. You're a storyteller, use those skills!

3) Your career is yours
The thing about startup and some crypto talent is that they often land in inflated titles or undefined roles - and have no idea how to package that experience or identify where they fit in a more structured org 

At the top of the hiring funnel, it is not the company's job to figure out who you are or where to put you. Being a CMO with two years' total experience is not the credibility booster that you think it is. Tell a different story (I am happy to help!)

4) The top is not nirvana
Real misery is faking your way through a job every day, worrying your CEO will realize you lack the basic skills of the team you manage

Stop applying for C-suite positions because it’s the next stop on the escalator. Forget about title. Apply for new experiences where you can stretch & learn, but where your skills are directly applicable today 

5) The take home test is a trap 
You don't have enough information to complete an entire strategic battery for a company. It will be wrong. Or too detailed to invite more questions than answers

An unpaid test is free work and a fishing expedition. It often shows that the hiring org does not know how to support or value the GTM function. Instead, give a day rate or offer to do a working session together, live, where you can see each other's work styles and demonstrate how you think in real time. You will lose opportunities by setting these boundaries but eventually you will also land in a better company
--

There are many stories right now of candidates being ghosted in offer stage and all sorts of bad behavior on the employer side, and it's not lost on me that being unemployed can be a demoralizing experience. But that doesn't change the fact that the higher value, healthier, better quality organizations are going to have competition, and they're going to be worth the fight. If this sounds unfair, remember fortune doesn't just favor the bold - it favors the realists who know what they're working with and where they need to tighten their game.

💰 VALUATION

Polymarket's only competitor with a live token is Opinion - $300M FDV, 20% circulating, and a massive disappointment for farmers. Over 95% of activity was over-farmed, metrics cratered post-TGE, and the team allocated a tiny supply to the drop. Opinion's current activity is ~20x lower than Polymarket's, even though they nearly matched at the points campaign peak.

Polymarket itself has an estimated 20–50% wash trade volume. Factor in the viral multiplier, and a $5–7B FDV at launch looks realistic.

But here's the catch: the project raised at a $9B valuation and is eyeing $20B. Rumors of an IPO aren't just rumors - pre-IPO allocations are already circulating privately at 30–40% premiums. If Polymarket launches both a token AND stock, valuation splits between the two.

My take: $5B FDV is the conservative token scenario. With no official IPO confirmation, a full tilt toward the token could push it to $10B+.

Circulating supply at TGE likely sits at 15–25%, meaning users could realistically see 7.5–15% of total supply. A standard 10% at $5B FDV = $500M airdrop for regular users. Ambitious but plausible in this market.

The CEO and CMO have been teasing the token, hinting at launch after Polymarket's legal return to the US — which already happened. The current benchmark is an intern's post: "1M markets and $POLY next." Hourly, 15-min, and 5-min markets are live. 1-minute markets are next.
